content.title: Persistent Matchup Strip | Causal Rally to a Visible Point
content.summary: Keep one fixed two-competitor identity strip visible while a single small object carries a serve, reception, counter and pressure exchange across changing shot scales. Recalibrate geography once from overhead, show the scoring state, then hold contrasting winner and loser reactions.

quick_start.input_format: fixed two-competitor matchup strip + established play axis + one causally continuous small-object rally + cut matching by object direction, striking side or body weight + one overhead recalibration + visible score outcome and opposed reactions
quick_start.recommended_input: Adult air-hockey competitors ORBIT in cobalt and TIDE in amber play one continuous glowing-puck point beneath a fixed lower matchup strip. Preserve puck direction across every cut, use one overhead rink view, show the puck entering ORBIT's goal, update the strip to 0-1 and hold TIDE's restrained raised fist against ORBIT's lowered paddle.
required_anchors: Keep one fixed two-competitor identity strip registered throughout the sequence.
Establish the play axis and both starting positions before the rally accelerates.
Use at least one overhead recalibration before the decisive exchange.
Show the scoring outcome and contrasting reactions before ending, with the identity strip still visible.
usage_steps: Replace the example subject, setting, and surface details with an original concept.
Keep every required anchor and Creative DNA invariant causally visible.
Choose the MiniMax H3 or Seedance 2.0 prompt and fill only the declared variable slots.
Check duration, event order, camera continuity, sound, and anti-copy constraints before generation.
applicable_scope: Keep one fixed two-competitor identity strip visible while a single small object carries a serve, reception, counter and pressure exchange across changing shot scales. Original 4–15 second concepts that can preserve every required anchor.

Long-form exposition or unrelated multi-location stories without a compact causal chain.

creative_dna.mechanism: Reserve one fixed identity strip for two original competitors, team colors and a compact matchup title; keep it registered through the entire sequence. In the action region, establish the play axis, then build one causally continuous rally through serve, reception, counter, pressure exchange and decisive contact. Every cut must inherit the small object's incoming direction, striking side or player weight shift; use at least one overhead view to recalibrate geography. End only after the object's landing or scoring state is visible, followed by contrasting winner and loser reactions while the identity strip persists. The reusable mechanism is persistent matchup orientation plus small-object causal continuity and terminal reaction—not the source countries, athletes, faces, uniforms, table, paddles, poster art, flags, words, exact rally, camera, crowd, creator identity or timing.

invariants.rule: Keep one fixed two-competitor identity strip registered throughout the sequence.
invariants.purpose: Prevents orientation loss during high-density cuts.
invariants.ablation_failure: If the strip moves or disappears, fast inserts can become anonymous highlights.

invariants.rule: Establish the play axis and both starting positions before the rally accelerates.
invariants.purpose: Gives each later direction a spatial reference.
invariants.ablation_failure: Close-ups without a baseline make returns impossible to parse.

invariants.rule: Carry every cut through incoming object direction, striking side or body-weight transfer.
invariants.purpose: Preserves one causal rally across changing shot scales.
invariants.ablation_failure: Unmatched ball motion turns the point into disconnected spectacle.

invariants.rule: Use at least one overhead recalibration before the decisive exchange.
invariants.purpose: Restores table or field geography as density peaks.
invariants.ablation_failure: Without recalibration, the terminal exchange loses positional meaning.

invariants.rule: Show the scoring outcome and contrasting reactions before ending, with the identity strip still visible.
invariants.purpose: Closes action, result and social interpretation together.
invariants.ablation_failure: Celebration without a result is unsupported; a result without reactions lacks payoff.

slots.name: sound_family
slots.constraint: An original hierarchy of diegetic cues; no unsupported source-audio claim.

anti_copy_exclusions: the source countries, national labels, flags, athlete faces, bodies, uniforms and exact team colors
the source table-tennis table, paddles, ball path, serves, dives, returns, celebration and crowd reactions
the source persistent poster art, typography, portraits, brush graphics, copy and lower-half layout
the source camera sequence, overheads, close-ups, exact 15-second rally timing and animation treatment
the source creator identity, Seedance 2.5 and GPT Image 2 claims, watermark, platform overlay and branding
